findings.failure_mode: A task that hits its hard time limit is stored as FAILURE and its errbacks and task_failure handlers fire. The message is then requeued and runs again. Users see FAILURE, then the task running again (and possibly SUCCESS later), and the errbacks fire once per redelivery.
findings.trigger_condition: acks_late=True with acks_on_timeout=False (or the legacy acks_on_failure_or_timeout=False), and a task that reliably runs past time_limit, e.g. because of a large input or a slow dependency
findings.amplifier: Each redelivery holds a pool slot for the whole hard time limit, then the child is killed and a new one has to be forked. on_failure skips mark_as_failure when the message is requeued (line 734), but on_timeout writes FAILURE and fires the hooks before it requeues, so the two paths disagree.
findings.sustaining_effect: The requeued message comes back at full cost with no attempt counter or cap. A deterministic overrun becomes a poison message that keeps using worker capacity and re-firing errbacks after the slow dependency has recovered, until someone purges the queue.
findings.blast_radius: Every task sharing the affected workers and queue loses capacity. Chords and workflows that react to the FAILURE result or the errbacks run their failure handling more than once.

evidence.note: mark_as_failure runs whether or not the message will be requeued
task.on_failure, task_failure signal and task-failed event fire before the ack/reject decision
reject(requeue=True) when acks_on_timeout is False: no redelivery cap
on_failure deliberately skips mark_as_failure when requeued; on_timeout does not
[fix] 'send the task failure in hard timeout' added the failure hooks ahead of the requeue branch
[feature] changed the timeout path from 'ack or nothing' to reject(requeue=True)

findings.confidence_rationale: The code clearly writes FAILURE and fires the hooks and then requeues. The [fix] commit 7135768 is the change that put the hooks ahead of the requeue. Defaults are acks_on_timeout=True (task.py:449-453), so only opt-in configurations hit this.
findings.how_to_verify: Set acks_late=True, acks_on_timeout=False, time_limit=1 on a task that sleeps 5s. Watch the broker redeliver it indefinitely while the result backend shows FAILURE and an errback counter increases on every attempt.
findings.prediction: A bug report about errbacks firing repeatedly, or a FAILURE result flipping to SUCCESS, for acks_late tasks with acks_on_timeout disabled

findings.failure_mode: When the result backend is unavailable, a task that raised Reject(requeue=False) is never rejected. The message stays unacked on the worker and is redelivered after the connection drops or the worker restarts. The task runs again and fails the same way. On-call sees duplicate executions and messages stuck as unacked.
findings.trigger_condition: Result backend outage or timeout (Redis or database down) while tasks raise Reject(requeue=False). Applies when result_backend_always_retry is off, so store_result raises.
findings.amplifier: mark_as_failure and the task_failure signal run before self.reject(). An exception in the backend write skips the reject, and the task_failure signal and event are lost as well.
findings.sustaining_effect: Each redelivery repeats the full task body and then hits the same backend write. While the backend is degraded, the backend load and the unacked backlog keep growing.
findings.blast_radius: Tasks that use Reject(requeue=False) on workers sharing the failing result backend. Unacked messages count against the prefetch limit and starve other tasks on that worker.

evidence.note: backend.mark_as_failure called before the message is settled
reject() only reached if the backend write and signal dispatch succeed
contrast: the generic acks_late path settles the message before writing to the backend
[feature] introduced the backend write ahead of reject() in the Reject branch

findings.confidence_rationale: The ordering is visible in the code. I did not read the backend retry configuration or how the pool callback handles an exception raised from on_failure, so whether the message stays unacked or the worker logs and moves on is inferred.
findings.how_to_verify: Point the result backend at a closed port with result_backend_always_retry=False. Run a task that raises Reject(requeue=False) and check that the message stays unacked and is redelivered after a worker restart.

findings.failure_mode: A task that kills its child process (OOM kill, segfault, or now SystemExit) is requeued forever when reject_on_worker_lost is set. Workers keep losing children and the same message keeps coming back.
findings.trigger_condition: reject_on_worker_lost=True with acks_late, and a payload that always crashes the child, e.g. memory blow-up on large input or a library calling sys.exit
findings.amplifier: Commit 67ba9e5 converts SystemExit/KeyboardInterrupt from a child that was not cancelled into WorkerLostError, so more exit causes now take the requeue branch. Nothing counts redeliveries.
findings.sustaining_effect: The requeued message is redelivered at full cost and kills another child each time. Pool capacity is spent re-forking processes until the message is purged.
findings.blast_radius: All tasks on queues consumed by the affected workers. Throughput drops while children are repeatedly killed and re-forked.

evidence.note: SystemExit and KeyboardInterrupt are mapped to WorkerLostError via _worker_lost_info
reject_on_worker_lost leads to reject(requeue=True) with no attempt limit
[feature] widened the worker-lost path to SystemExit reports

findings.confidence_rationale: The requeue-without-cap is clear in the code. The docs warn about it for reject_on_worker_lost, but the newer SystemExit mapping widens the trigger. I did not confirm how billiard reports these exits.
findings.how_to_verify: Set acks_late=True and reject_on_worker_lost=True on a task that calls os._exit(1) or sys.exit(1). Count how often the broker redelivers it within a minute.

notes: Also considered: on_failure re-raises MemoryError in the parent process (line 676), which skips both the ack/reject and the backend write. Left out because I could not confirm how the pool callback handles the re-raised exception. The fix/revert pair a7d9c79/a6bc479 (chord hang on revoke) shows the revoke-to-backend path in _announce_revoked is unsettled, but the reverted code is gone and nothing that fails remains to cite.
